rows.form_factor: Handheld iPhone Pro/Pro Max from 12 Pro; iPad Pro from 2020
rows.weight_power: iPad Pro 11-inch (2020) cited at 471 g. iPhone mass and LiDAR power unknown.
rows.range: Apple 2020: up to 5 m. Polycam processing cap 5 m.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Not TLS. Apple publishes no mm accuracy. iPhone 12 Pro / 15 Pro RMSE vs primitives 2.05 cm and 2.06 cm (Remote Sensing Letters 2026). iPad Pro SiteScape vs TLS ICP RMS ~2 cm ± 3 cm (ISPRS 2021).
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Poor as sole sensor for ~0.12 deg / few-mm tip offset. Centimeter error exceeds derived 8 ft offset.
rows.cost_availability: Consumer Pro devices. ARKit depth; app smoothing unknown vs raw.

rows.form_factor: iOS app. Space Mode LiDAR vs non-LiDAR photogrammetry.
rows.weight_power: Phone. Cloud preset uses Polycam servers. Power unknown.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Help Center says up to 98% under optimal conditions. Not an RMSE. Do not convert to mm.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Same limit as S1. Named Photo/Detail hybrid mode not found.
rows.cost_availability: Point-cloud export (LAS, PLY, PTS, XYZ, DXF) is Business and Enterprise. Free is GLTF only.

rows.form_factor: Tripod TLS. Examples FARO Focus Premium, Leica RTC360, Leica BLK360 SE.
rows.weight_power: RTC360 5.2 kg without batteries; battery 340 g; typically up to 4 h. FARO and BLK360 SE mass unknown here.
rows.range: FARO Focus Premium white 90% 0.5-200 m (Max 0.5-400 m). RTC360 0.5-130 m. BLK360 SE 0.5-45 m.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Vendor claims. FARO 3D accuracy 2 mm @ 10 m, angular 19 arcsec. RTC360 1.9 mm @ 10 m, angular 18 arcsec. BLK360 SE 4 mm @ 10 m.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Only class with published specs at millimeter / sub-0.1 deg order. End-to-end stud angle on site unknown.
rows.cost_availability: Professional capital equipment. Street price unknown.

rows.form_factor: Overlapping photos; Polycam non-LiDAR mode; Pix4D-class processing.
rows.range: No single range. Set by baseline and GSD.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Pix4D: GCPs raise absolute accuracy; no universal mm RMSE published.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Unknown. Not assumed better than phone LiDAR without control.
rows.cost_availability: Phone photos cheap. Pix4D commercial. Polycam point export needs Business/Enterprise.

rows.form_factor: Optical see-through glasses plus compute puck. Two tracking cameras, one high-res camera, 6DoF.
rows.weight_power: Official page omits grams. Puck battery 4455 mAh, 34.84 Wh. Secondary review under 95 g / 270 g puck is unverified.
rows.range: Survey range unknown. Display FOV 70 deg.
rows.precision_vs_tls: No depth RMSE on the official page.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Display, not capture scanner. Unsuitable as the metrology sensor.
rows.cost_availability: Base model not more than US$1500 before tax. Fall 2026 launch.

rows.weight_power: Unknown. Stereolabs spec sheet not opened.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Unknown. Dataset does not state accuracy.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Controlled single-stud capture. Not evidence of 0.12 deg wall plumb.

rows.precision_vs_tls: Vendor: fine ranging < 10 cm. White paper: ~30 cm spatial resolution at 500 MHz.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Not suitable. Resolution cell much larger than a stud face.

rows.form_factor: 60 GHz FMCW module with onboard DSP.
rows.weight_power: TIDEP-01000 short-range config: 2 W. Mass unknown.
rows.range: Short-range people-counting config: 8.1 m; FOV 120 deg horizontal, 40 deg vertical.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Reference design: people localized to ±10 cm. Range resolution 8.4 cm. Static-clutter removal in area-scanner demo.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Not suitable for mm-class stud edges.
Not relevant. Listed because the brief cited the PII.

rows.form_factor: Handheld iPhone Pro / iPad Pro. No separate LiDAR SKU.
rows.weight_power: iPad Pro 11-inch (2020) cited at 471 g. iPhone mass and LiDAR power unknown.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Not TLS. Peer RMSE about 2.05-2.06 cm (Remote Sensing Letters 2026). See S1.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: Apple publishes no mm spec. iPhone 12 Pro / 15 Pro RMSE vs primitives 2.05 cm and 2.06 cm.
rows.angular_implication: Derived single-point equivalent: 20 mm over 8 ft (2438.4 mm) is about 0.47 deg. Fitted-axis error cannot be derived.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: No for a 0.12 deg call. ARKit can name gravity (W30); ranging error still dominates.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: No. Centimeter surface error exceeds the about 5 mm tip budget.
rows.price_band_usd: No separate sensor price. Phone street price not fetched. Unverified.
rows.cost_availability: Consumer Pro devices. Dollar band unverified this pass.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip as the QA sensor. Useful for rough capture and demos.

rows.modality: Livox mid-range hybrid solid-state (Mid-360, Mid-70, Avia)
rows.form_factor: Small hybrid solid-state modules for robots. Ethernet and external DC.
rows.weight_power: Mid-360: 265 g, 6.5 W average, self-heat peak 14 W, 9-27 V. Mid-70: 580 g, 8 W, 10-15 V. Avia: 498 g, 8-9 W, 10-15 V.
rows.range: Mid-360: 40 m at 10% reflectivity, 70 m at 80%. Mid-70: 90 m at 10%, 260 m at 80% (100 klx). Avia: 190 m at 10% and 320 m at 80% under 100 klx; 450 m at 80% and 0 klx.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Centimeter range precision, not TLS. Mid-360 angular precision < 0.15 deg. Avia < 0.05 deg. Mid-70 < 0.1 deg.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: Mid-360 range precision (1 sigma) <= 2 cm at 10 m (80% reflectivity, 25 C) and <= 3 cm at 0.2 m. Mid-70 <= 2 cm at 20 m (30% reflectivity). Avia 2 cm at 20 m (80% reflectivity).
rows.angular_implication: Derived single-point equivalent of 2 cm over 8 ft is about 0.47 deg. Mid-360 < 0.15 deg ray spec is 6.4 mm of tip over 8 ft, coarser than 0.12 deg. Avia < 0.05 deg is 2.1 mm of tip, but the 2 cm range term still dominates as a bias. Fitted angle cannot be derived.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: No for 0.12 deg. Partial only for seeing lumber if the sensor dwells.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: No plumb call. Mid-360 IMU ICM40609 and Avia IMU BMI088 can name an up vector. Mid-70 spec page lists no IMU. Not a survey compensator. Thin or low-reflectivity targets within 1 m are not guaranteed on Mid-360.
rows.price_band_usd: Mid-360 official trial sample USD 749 on 2023-01-10. Current Livox list not shown (DJI store region unavailable). Third-party street USD 899 on 2026-09-23 (AIFITLAB, Robotics Center), not a Livox list. Mid-70 DJI Store USD 1429 out of stock (fetched 2026-09-23). Avia DJI Store USD 2079 out of stock (same day).
rows.cost_availability: Hundreds to about two thousand USD. Mid-70 and Avia were out of stock on the DJI pages fetched.
rows.power_mount: Robot or tripod plus external DC. Not a leveled scan head. Mid-360 FOV 360 deg by -7 to +52 deg.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip for the red/green call. Cheapest robotics class, published errors not inside the framing tolerance.

rows.weight_power: 800 g side connector or 900 g bottom connector. 10 W typical (room temperature, 12 V, 600 rpm). Supply should provide at least 30 W. DC 9-36 V.
rows.range: Instrumented 0.05-120 m. 80 m at 10% reflectivity on channels 9-24; 50 m at 10% on the other channels.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Better than Livox range precision, still not TLS. Vertical resolution 1 deg.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: Ranging accuracy +/-1 cm typical, +/-2 cm standard. Precision 0.5 cm typical (1 sigma), 2 cm standard. Typical: channels 9-24, outdoors, 0.5-70 m, 30 C, 50% reflectivity. User manual X01, file date 2026-05-10.
rows.angular_implication: Derived single-point equivalent: 10 mm over 8 ft is about 0.235 deg. 5 mm precision is about 0.117 deg, the whole tolerance, and only if that 5 mm is the entire stud error. Ring spacing at 3 m from the stated 1 deg resolution is about 52 mm.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: No for plumb. Partial for horizontal sampling versus a 16-beam puck.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: No. Spec table lists GNSS/PTP and no IMU. No dual-axis compensator found. 1 deg rings are coarse for a stud edge.
rows.price_band_usd: Not in the manual. Street price unverified.
rows.power_mount: Ethernet. Vertical FOV 31 deg (-16 to +15), so one pose does not cover an 8 ft wall at a few meters.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip until a wood-stud test and a price exist. A systematic 1 cm error is outside 0.12 deg.

rows.modality: Mapping-grade spinning lidar (Ouster OS1 Rev8, Velodyne VLP-16)
rows.form_factor: 360 deg spinning imaging lidars for robotics and mapping.
rows.weight_power: OS1: 500 g without cap, 580 g with halo cap, 10-20 W (15 W nominal) at 1024x10 Hz, 9-58 V. VLP-16: about 830 g without cable or interface box, 8 W typical, 9-18 V with interface box.
rows.range: OS1: 90 m at 10% Lambertian, 170 m at 80%, 1024 at 10 Hz, >90% detection, 100 klx. Vertical FOV 44 deg. VLP-16: 100 m, vertical FOV 30 deg.
rows.precision_vs_tls: OS1 range accuracy is centimeter-class. Angular sampling accuracy +/-0.01 deg is much finer than 0.12 deg and is not the binding term. VLP-16 is +/-3 cm typical with 2.0 deg vertical resolution.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: OS1 Rev8 datasheet (rev 08/03/2026): range precision min +/-0.25 cm, max +/-1.5 cm (1 sigma, typical, beyond 1 m, 1024 at 10 Hz). Range accuracy +/-1.25 cm Lambertian, +/-2.5 cm retroreflective. VLP-16 Rev-H (2018): range accuracy up to +/-3 cm typical.
rows.angular_implication: Derived: 12.5 mm over 8 ft is about 0.29 deg. OS1 +/-0.01 deg sampling is 0.43 mm of tip over 8 ft. Equal-beam illustration only: 128 channels over 44 deg is about 0.35 deg and about 18 mm at 3 m; the datasheet does not say beams are equal. VLP-16: 30 mm over 8 ft is about 0.70 deg; 2.0 deg ring spacing at 3 m is about 105 mm.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: VLP-16 no for stud edges (about 10 cm between rings at 3 m) and no IMU on the spec sheet. OS1 partial on edge sampling at 64 or 128 channels; synchronous IMU IAM-20685HP; no survey compensator found.
rows.price_band_usd: OS1 quote only (Ouster how-to-buy). Street unverified. VLP-16 introductory USD 7999 in 2014. Current price unverified.
rows.cost_availability: Commercial. OS1 not publicly listed. VLP-16 current street unverified.
rows.power_mount: Vehicle, robot, or tripod with external power and gigabit or 100 Mbps Ethernet. OS1 vertical FOV +/-22 deg.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip. Mapping lidars are the wrong product for a few-millimeter plumb call.

rows.form_factor: One-button imaging scanner on a tripod or a surface. Internal battery.
rows.weight_power: 0.75 kg without battery. GEB825 battery 0.1 kg. 10 W typical, 16 W max. Internal 7.4 V battery.
rows.range: 0.5-45 m. Full dome 360 deg horizontal by 270 deg vertical. Up to 680,000 points/s.
rows.precision_vs_tls: 3D point accuracy is a few millimeters, close to survey TLS, but the tilt spec is arcminutes not arcseconds.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: User manual v1.4: 3D point accuracy 4 mm at 10 m and 8 mm at 20 m (1 sigma, 78% albedo). Range noise 1 mm at 10 m at 78% albedo. Tilt: IMU based, 8 arcmin in a working range; +/-5 deg for upright and upside-down.
rows.angular_implication: Derived: 4 mm over 8 ft is about 0.094 deg. The tilt spec is 8 arcmin = 0.133 deg, about 5.7 mm of tip over 8 ft, which is not inside 0.12 deg (7.2 arcmin). Tilt is the binding spec and is quoted, not derived.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Partial. Dense sampling can see a stud. The published tilt spec misses 0.12 deg.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: Partial. Dense+ is 6 mm spacing at 10 m. Gravity reference is the 8 arcmin IMU, not the Cyclone DAC list (RTC360, P-series, C-series). Wood is not the 78% albedo surface.
rows.price_band_usd: Leica US shop overview search extract on 2026-09-23 showed USD 26500. Direct fetch returned HTTP 403. Unverified against a live cart.
rows.cost_availability: Leica shop extract about USD 26500, live confirmation unverified.
rows.power_mount: Tripod or surface. VIS tracks motion between setups and does not work in complete darkness.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip for the plumb call. Cheaper tripod scanner than survey TLS, but 8 arcmin tilt is outside 0.12 deg.

rows.modality: Survey TLS class (FARO Focus Premium, Leica RTC360). Specs also in S3.
rows.form_factor: Tripod phase or time-of-flight scanner with inclinometer or dual-axis compensator.
rows.weight_power: RTC360: 5.2 kg nominal without batteries; battery 340 g; typically up to 4 h. Focus mass unknown on the pages read for S3.
rows.range: Focus Premium white 90% 0.5-200 m. RTC360 0.5-130 m. See S3.
rows.precision_vs_tls: This is the reference class. Focus 3D accuracy 2 mm at 10 m, angular accuracy 19 arcsec. RTC360 1.9 mm at 10 m, angular 18 arcsec.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: Vendor claims, 1 sigma. Focus Premium: 3D accuracy 2 mm at 10 m, ranging error +/-1 mm, angular accuracy 19 arcsec. RTC360: 3D point accuracy 1.9 mm at 10 m, range accuracy 1.0 mm + 10 ppm, angular 18 arcsec.
rows.angular_implication: Derived single-point equivalent: 2 mm over 8 ft is about 0.047 deg; 1.9 mm is about 0.045 deg. 19 arcsec of tip over 8 ft is about 0.22 mm. Angle spec is far inside 0.12 deg. Fitted stud error on wood cannot be derived.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Yes on instrument specs. Registration, wood reflectance, occlusion, and box-fit error are not in the brochure.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: Yes for edges at indoor ranges relative to robotics lidars. FARO inclinometer can be used in SCENE if the scanner stays within +/-5 deg. Cyclone REGISTER 360 treats RTC360 and P/C-series as high-accuracy leveled / DAC scans.
rows.price_band_usd: Focus: public FARO quotation 02280272 dated 2023-04-24, expired 2023-09-30, listed Focus Premium at USD 41860 list and 39767 after discount. Not a 2026 list. RTC360 LT: Leica shop catalog extract on 2026-09-23 showed USD 68096. Live cart unverified.
rows.cost_availability: Professional capital equipment. Current Focus street price unverified. RTC360 LT shop extract USD 68096 unverified live.
rows.power_mount: Tripod. See S3 for RTC360 battery life. Not a robot puck.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Viable class for OpenWall. Lowest class whose published ranging and angular specs both sit inside about 0.12 deg. Not the lowest dollar in the table.

rows.modality: Handheld / backpack SLAM (FARO Orbis Premium, GeoSLAM ZEB Horizon)
rows.form_factor: Walking SLAM scanner. Orbis: handheld, monopod, backpack, or car mount. Any orientation.
rows.weight_power: Orbis Premium tech sheet: scanner 2.10 kg, datalogger 0.95 kg, battery 0.55 kg, about 3 h. Horizon FARO sheet: scanner 1.45 kg.
rows.range: Orbis 120 m, 32 channels, FOV 360 by 290 deg, 640,000 points/s. Horizon 100 m, 16 sensors, 300,000 points/s, FOV 360 by 270 deg.
rows.precision_vs_tls: Vendor precision can look millimeter-class. It is relative or SLAM precision, not a TLS 3D-accuracy-plus-compensator spec.
rows.ranging_or_accuracy: Orbis Premium sheet revised 2025-06-10: mobile precision 5 mm (1 sigma), stationary Flash precision 2 mm (1 sigma). Horizon FARO sheet: relative accuracy up to 6 mm in GeoSLAM Connect V2. A 2024 paper quotes the Zeb Horizon manufacturer at 0.01-0.03 m relative. Those Horizon figures disagree. No stud-plumb test found.
rows.angular_implication: Derived single-point equivalents: 5 mm over 8 ft is about 0.117 deg, 2 mm is about 0.047 deg, 6 mm is about 0.141 deg. Not a proof the trajectory is plumb.
rows.stud_plumb_suitability: Partial. Flash 2 mm is in the survey-TLS order as a vendor precision. Mobile mode is the whole tip budget and is relative.
rows.stud_edges_gravity: Partial on edges in Flash mode (19M points, 13 mm at 10 m). Sheet does not say cloud Z is gravity. Any-orientation use is the opposite of a leveled tripod.
rows.price_band_usd: Not on the FARO sheets read here. Reseller prices were not used. Street price unverified.
rows.cost_availability: Commercial SLAM kits. Official street price unverified.
rows.power_mount: Handheld or backpack. Backpack mounting does not change the accuracy class.
rows.price_vs_accuracy: Skip for a purchase decision. No official price shows stationary Flash undercuts survey TLS, and mobile precision is not a gravity-plumb spec.
